script: I still do not know if she did it on purpose. Forty one minutes. That is how long my mother-in-law left me inside the family group chat, and I read seven years of it. I did not scroll. I read. There is a difference. I found that out in a car park with the engine still running and my son asleep in the back. They had a name for me. Two syllables. I am not going to say it out loud. They had a name for the way I laugh. There is a message from my sister-in-law, from the morning of my father's funeral, and it has four likes on it. My husband defended me twice in seven years. Twice. And both times he did it with an emoji. And then, about forty minutes in, I reached the top. The first message. And the group was not called the family. It had my name on it. She made it eleven days after we got engaged. For seven years it did exactly what she built it to do. There is one more thing. My father in law is in that chat. He said almost nothing for four years and they all called him cold. He never came to a single Sunday lunch. He sent me a birthday card every year signed only by him, never from the two of them, and he was the only person in that house who used my name instead of the girl. His last message is three years old. It says, I am out. This is not a family, it is a committee. Then he left. And nobody has said his name at a table since. Three years I sat at Christmas thinking he was the one who could not stand me. He was the only one who could. She took me out after forty one minutes. She sent a laughing face. Wrong chat, sorry. I sent one back. I go to Christmas. I have never told a soul what I read. I have never told anybody why he left. I tell people she added me by mistake.

title: 41 minutes inside the family group chat, and I read seven years of it
description:
Seven years of messages. I did not scroll, I read, and there is a difference.

Forty minutes in I got to the very first message, and the group was not called the family. It had my name on it.

My father-in-law left that group three years ago. Nobody ever mentioned it, and for three years I thought he was the one who did not like me.

What would you have done with those forty one minutes?
